title: Give an object a material and a color
summary: Create a new material in the Properties editor, set its Base Color and preview it in the viewport.

steps.say: In Object Mode, click the monkey head you added earlier so it has an orange outline.

checks.prompt: Is one object in the 3D viewport outlined in orange, showing it is selected?

hints: Click Suzanne in the Outliner at the top right if it is hard to hit in the view.
No monkey yet? Press Shift A, point at Mesh, and click Monkey.
steps.why: A material is added to the selected object.

steps.say: In the Properties editor at the bottom right, click the Material tab, the red checkered sphere.

checks.prompt: Does the Properties editor now show material settings, with either a New button or a material name at the top?

hints: Hover over the icons in the narrow column on the left edge of the Properties editor. A tooltip names each tab.
The Material tab is right below the green triangle of the Data tab.
steps.why: All surface settings for the selected object live in the Material tab.

steps.say: Click New to create a material.

checks.prompt: Does the Material tab now show a material named Material with a Surface panel listing Principled BSDF?

hints: New is a wide button with a plus sign near the top of the Material tab.
If you see a material name instead of New, this object already has a material. Say done and go on.
steps.why: A new material starts with the Principled BSDF shader, which covers most surfaces.

steps.say: In the Surface panel, click the color bar next to Base Color.

check.prompt: Is a color picker popup with a color wheel open over the Properties editor?

hints: Base Color is one of the first settings under Principled BSDF. The bar is light gray.
Scroll down inside the Properties editor if the Surface panel is out of view.
steps.why: Base Color is the main color of the surface.

steps.say: Click a strong color in the wheel, such as red or blue, then move the mouse away to close the picker.

checks.prompt: Is the bar next to Base Color now a clear color instead of light gray?

hints: The slider beside the wheel sets brightness. Drag it up if the color looks black.
You can also type a color code in the Hex field of the picker.
steps.why: The color is stored in the material, so every object using it changes together.

steps.say: With your mouse over the 3D viewport, press Z and choose Material Preview.

checks.prompt: Does the selected object in the 3D viewport now show the chosen color with soft lighting and reflections?

hints: Z opens a round menu around the pointer. Material Preview is one of its options.
Or click the third of the four sphere icons at the right end of the viewport header.
steps.why: Solid view ignores materials. Material Preview shows them with sample lighting.
